candidates.spoken: Liberty ships cracked and some broke in two.
Liberty ships failed because brittle fracture in welded hulls.
Cracks started at sharp corners and weld defects.
It took only welded steel turning brittle in cold seas.
A welded hull is one piece.
Metallurgist Constance Tipper showed how the steel failed.
Welding wasn't the mistake on its own.
They were Liberty ships, built fast by welding.
Steel toughness then became a basic design requirement.
Constance Tipper's research made steel toughness a design requirement.
In cold water, their steel turned brittle.
A few suddenly split completely in two.
It started with hulls welded for speed. It ended with hull splits.

script.spoken: Liberty ships cracked and some broke in two. A few suddenly split completely in two, even at the dock. They were Liberty ships, built fast by welding. In cold water, their steel turned brittle. Cracks started at sharp corners and weld defects. A welded hull is one piece, so a crack had nothing to stop it. Metallurgist Constance Tipper showed how the steel failed. Steel toughness then became a basic design requirement.
